LESSON: GROWING TREES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Growing trees
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Growing trees, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can growing trees conserve the environment? 2. Why is growing trees important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Growing trees together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: The learner develops skills in interacting with digital technology as they use digital devices to watch captioned video clips

on the importance of trees.

• Self-efficacy: The learner develops leadership skills when they share and carry out tasks in groups to establish a tree of their choice.

• Citizenship: The learner demonstrates responsibility and care for the environment by planting trees for environmental conservation.

Values:
Responsibility: As the learner diligently plants a tree seed or seedling and takes care of it until it is fully established.

13

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Environmental education and climate change: The learner promotes environmental conservation by planting a tree seed or seedling and

taking care of it until it is fully established.

● Safety and security: The learner observes safety and security for self and others as they use garden tools and equipment to plant trees.

Link to other learning areas:

Learners relate tree planting to conservation of natural resources learnt in social studies.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Digital devices and print materials.

• Seeds of trees.

• Tree Seedlings.

• Organic manure.

• Mulching materials
